adds.title: Persecution of transgender people under the second Trump administration (Wikipedia, prison-segregation section)
adds.summary: Federal-prison housing layer (Bureau of Prisons custody, where District-sentenced felons serve): the article documents that Executive Order 14168 (January 20, 2025) rescinded EO 13988, which had protected LGBTQ rights in federal prisons. From 2025 the Federal Bureau of Prisons stopped reporting the number of transgender prisoners held; beginning in 2026 it adopted Florida-style policies under which transgender inmates would have hair cut short, be taken off hormone medication, and be placed in psychiatric therapy. Bureau of Justice Assistance deputy director Tammie Gregg confirmed prison (PREA) inspection guidance was changed to align practices in prisons with EO 14168 (trans-related standards marked 'not applicable'), which Just Detention International executive director Linda McFarlane said 'will immediately put people in danger'.

adds.title: Executive Order 14168 (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Placement outcome of EO 14168 ('Defending Women from Gender Ideology Extremity and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government', signed January 20, 2025): its federal-prison directives ban transgender women from women's federal prisons (The Advocate: 'Donald Trump bans transgender women from women's prisons'), and HRC and the ACLU reported transgender women being transferred to men's prisons, told they would be, or moved to solitary confinement, with over 2,000 trans people in federal custody affected. The Bureau of Prisons stopped reporting the number of imprisoned transgender people as a result of the order; advocates argued it violates the Prison Rape Elimination Act's case-by-case housing rule and the ADA, while HRC's legal director said court orders granting inmates gender-affirming care remain in effect.

records.note: No District-specific housing data for its own DOC jail found within budget; documented prison-housing layer for the jurisdiction is federal, since DC-sentenced felons serve in Bureau of Prisons (BOP) custody. Findings verified: EO 14168 (Jan 20, 2025) requires federal prisons to house trans people by birth sex - transgender women transferred to or told they would be moved to men's prisons, some placed in solitary confinement; BOP stopped reporting trans-prisoner numbers from 2025 and from 2026 barred trans care (hair cut, off hormones, psychiatric therapy); PREA guidance aligned with EO 14168. Wikipedia full-text search returned only national articles (LGBTQ people in prison; Persecution of transgender people under the second Trump administration; Transgender rights in the United States) - no DC-specific placement, special-unit, or segregation rule found. Adds: 2 verified.

adds.title: Inmate at women's prison files suit over housing of transgender prisoner (Sun Journal, Mark LaFlamme)
adds.summary: Documented Maine case on identity-based placement: on April 3, 2026 the Lewiston Sun Journal reported that Katie Mountain, 41, an inmate at the Maine women's prison in Windham, filed a 30-page suit through attorney Cynthia Dill against Maine DOC Commissioner Randall Liberty, Warden Ben Beal and her former cellmate Andrea Balcer - a transgender woman and convicted double murderer held in the female facility. Mountain and nearly a dozen other women reported being groped, harassed, sexually propositioned and assaulted by Balcer, and Mountain says she was punished by staff for complaining. Outcome: the lawsuit contests the housing arrangement of the transgender prisoner in the women's prison.

adds.title: Persecution of transgender people under the second Trump administration (Wikipedia, prison-segregation section)
adds.summary: Maine placement practice documented: in April 2025, after the Maine Department of Corrections refused to move a transgender inmate to an opposite-gender prison, Attorney General Pam Bondi claimed on Fox & Friends that $1.5 million in federal funding was being withheld from the Maine Department of Corrections in response (the article cites WMTW, April 11, 2025, and WGME, April 16, 2025 reports). Outcome: Maine maintained identity-consistent housing for the trans inmate and faced a federal funding-cut threat, marking the documented conflict over birth-sex vs identity placement in Maine prisons.

records.note: Maine documented practice: transgender prisoners are housed by gender identity - the trans woman Andrea Balcer is held in the women's prison (Maine Correctional Center, Windham) alongside birth-female inmates. In April 2025 the Maine DOC refused to move a transgender inmate to an opposite-gender prison, prompting AG Pam Bondi's claim that $1.5M in federal funding was withheld in response; in April 2026 inmate Katie Mountain (via attorney Cynthia Dill) sued the MDOC commissioner, warden and cellmate Balcer over chronic harassment/assault by the transgender prisoner - directly contesting the identity-based housing arrangement. No Maine DOC special unit or solitary/segregation practice for trans prisoners documented within budget. Wikipedia search surfaced the case via the Cynthia Dill article citing the Sun Journal report; fetches: Sun Journal (ok), WMTW (blocked, 'Site Not Available' - dropped, not looped). Adds: 2 verified.
